name: Fujirebio Diagnostics, Inc
old_description: Fujirebio drives the biomarker-to-IVD journey – from pioneering research and scientific innovation through clinical validation on our platforms to global sharing in CDMO partnerships – ensuring transformative diagnostic solutions reach patients everywhere.
about:
Fujirebio Diagnostics, Inc. is headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania, and operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of Japan’s H.U. Group Holdings Inc. The company’s founding year and original founders are not disclosed in public materials.

The company develops and manufactures in vitro diagnostic (IVD) products, including the fully automated Lumipulse® platform, assay kits for neurodegenerative and other conditions, instruments, software, controls, and raw materials. It also operates as a contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO), offering partners end-to-end services from biomarker research through clinical validation, regulatory submission, and commercial production. Specific facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not published.

Fujirebio serves the global diagnostics industry, supplying hospitals, reference laboratories, and other IVD manufacturers. Its product portfolio spans neurology (Alzheimer’s, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson’s, ALS), oncology, infectious disease, autoimmune disorders, cardiac markers, diabetes, fertility, and transplantation. Recent collaborations include a letter of intent with Alzinova for a blood-based Alzheimer’s test and a sales partnership with Sysmex for dementia testing. Regulatory clearances include FDA-cleared biomarkers for blood-based Alzheimer’s diagnosis, CE marking for pTau 217 and NfL assays, Health Canada Class II licenses, and ANVISA authorization in Brazil.

Fujirebio emphasizes an open partnership model, providing diagnostic raw materials, reagents, and full development-to-manufacturing services to other technology providers. The company states that revenues from these partnerships are reinvested into R&D to fuel its innovation engine, aiming to multiply breakthroughs across diagnostic platforms and reach more patients than it could alone.
